## Goal

<!-- What this task achieves for the thesis. One or two sentences. -->

## Background

<!-- Domain knowledge needed for this issue to make sense.
     Link to papers, files, issues for deeper reading. -->

## Context

<!-- Why this constitutes progress toward the thesis (#1).
     What does completing this unblock or improve?
     Desired benefits and anticipated risks to the project.
     Reference parent issues. -->

## Deliverable

<!-- What the agent produces. Interaction surface with the rest
     of the project. Don't prescribe form — agent decides
     files, structure, commits. -->

## Scope

<!-- Agreed-upon boundaries. What's in, what's out.
     Prevents scope creep during implementation. -->

## Sources

<!-- Where to find information needed for implementation.
     Papers, code, specs. Flag trustworthiness where relevant.
     (Background = read to understand. Sources = read to implement.) -->

## Acceptance criteria

<!-- Measurable criteria, each with a motivation.
     External: the deliverable serves the project — downstream agents/code can use it.
     Internal: quality bar for long-term project health — clarity, correctness,
     review requirements per crates/CLAUDE.md. -->

## Notes

<!-- Preliminary findings from scoping/triage. Known risks inside scope.
     Suggested sub-issues worth considering. Can be empty for fresh issues. -->

## Open questions

<!-- Uncertainties, decisions for Jörn, dependencies on other issues.
     Resolve via edits as answers emerge. Once empty + Jörn approves,
     task is ready for assignment. -->
